help.intro: A scene of about one and a half minutes in a doctor's practice: a patient has a headache and a sore throat, the receptionist asks for his insurance card, and the doctor asks what hurts, since when, and whether he has a fever. At the end there is a Krankschreibung, the sick note every German employee knows. The scene is invented; the procedure is the real one in a German practice. You hear what you have just learnt: the body (der Kopf, der Hals, der Bauch, die Ohren), the pattern Mein Kopf tut weh / Meine Ohren tun weh, the possessives (mein, Ihr, Ihre), and the modal verbs müssen and dürfen in the doctor's advice. Listen once for the whole scene, then once for each symptom and each instruction.
help.tips[0].title: Saying what hurts
help.tips[0].text: X tut weh = X hurts; plural: X tun weh. Mein Kopf tut weh. Mein Hals tut weh. Meine Ohren tun weh. Or with Schmerzen: Ich habe Kopfschmerzen, Halsschmerzen, Bauchschmerzen. Fever: Ich habe Fieber, 38,5 (achtunddreißig fünf). Other useful lines: Mir ist schlecht (I feel sick), Ich bin müde, Ich habe Husten (cough), Ich habe Schnupfen (a cold).
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: My head hurts, and my throat hurts too.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: Do you have a fever? Yes, 38.5.
help.tips[0].check.why: Ohren is plural, so the verb is plural: tun weh.
help.tips[1].title: Possessives: mein, Ihr, Ihre
help.tips[1].text: mein (my) and Ihr (your, polite) take the same endings as ein: mein Kopf (der), mein Fieber (das), meine Hand (die), meine Ohren (plural). Ihre Versichertenkarte (die Karte), Ihr Name (der Name), Ihre Hände (plural). In the accusative masculine: meinen Kopf, Ihren Namen. Capital I for the polite Ihr, small i for ihr = her/their.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: Do you have your insurance card? Yes, here is my card.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: Please open your mouth. Your throat is red.
help.tips[1].check.why: der Name is masculine nominative: Ihr Name. Ihre would be feminine or plural.
help.remember[0]: Mein Kopf tut weh, meine Ohren tun weh; Ich habe Kopfschmerzen / Fieber / Husten.
help.remember[1]: mein / Ihr like ein: mein Kopf, meine Hand, Ihre Karte, Ihren Mund (accusative).
help.exam: Short scenes at the doctor's with symptoms and instructions are a typical listening task at this level.
help.hook: Headache, sore throat, 38.5 fever: listen to a visit to a German doctor, from the insurance card to the sick note.
passageTranslation:
Reception: Good morning. Do you have an appointment?
Patient: No, but I am ill. My head hurts, and my throat hurts too.
Reception: No problem. What is your name?
Patient: David Okafor.
Reception: Do you have your insurance card?
Patient: Yes, here is my card.
Reception: Thank you. Please take a seat in the waiting room. It will take about twenty minutes.
Doctor: Mr Okafor? Come in, please. What is wrong?
Patient: My head hurts, my throat hurts, and I am very tired.
Doctor: Since when?
Patient: Since Monday. So for three days.
Doctor: Do you have a fever?
Patient: Yes, this morning 38.5.
Doctor: Please open your mouth. Yes, your throat is very red. Do your ears hurt too?
Patient: No, my ears are okay. But I have a cough.
Doctor: That is a cold with fever. You must drink a lot, tea or water, and sleep a lot. You may not work for three days. I am writing you off sick.
Patient: Do I need medicine?
Doctor: I am giving you a prescription for tablets against the sore throat. Take one tablet in the morning and one in the evening. The pharmacy is right next door.
Patient: Thank you. And the sick note?
Doctor: You get that at reception. It goes automatically to your health insurance. For your boss you get a paper. Get well soon, Mr Okafor!
Patient: Thank you very much. Goodbye.
questions[0].explanation: "Mein Kopf tut weh, und mein Hals tut auch weh."
questions[1].explanation: "Haben Sie Ihre Versichertenkarte? Ja, hier ist meine Karte."
questions[1].questionTranslation: What does the reception want to see?
questions[1].optionsTranslation[0]: the passport or the identity card
questions[2].explanation: "Bitte nehmen Sie im Wartezimmer Platz. Es dauert etwa zwanzig Minuten."
questions[2].questionTranslation: How long must the patient wait in the waiting room?
questions[2].optionsTranslation[3]: he does not have to wait
questions[3].explanation: "Seit wann? Seit Montag. Also seit drei Tagen."
questions[3].questionTranslation: Since when has the patient been ill?
questions[3].optionsTranslation[1]: since Monday, so for three days
questions[3].optionsTranslation[2]: for a week, so since last Wednesday
questions[4].explanation: Possessives take -e in the plural: meine Ohren. das Ohr itself is neuter (mein Ohr).
questions[4].questionTranslation: 'My ears are okay.' Why meine and not mein?
questions[5].explanation: "Sie müssen viel trinken, Tee oder Wasser, und viel schlafen."
questions[5].optionsTranslation[0]: work a lot and sleep little
questions[5].optionsTranslation[1]: drink a lot and sleep a lot
questions[6].explanation: nicht dürfen = not allowed. The doctor forbids work for three days and writes him off sick.
questions[6].questionTranslation: 'You may not work for three days.' What does that mean?
questions[6].optionsTranslation[0]: He cannot work because he currently has no job and no boss.
questions[6].optionsTranslation[1]: He should not work; the doctor does not allow it.
questions[6].optionsTranslation[2]: He must work for three days.
questions[6].optionsTranslation[3]: He does not want to work.
questions[7].explanation: "Nehmen Sie eine Tablette am Morgen und eine am Abend."
questions[7].questionTranslation: How often does the patient take the tablets?
questions[7].optionsTranslation[0]: one in the morning and one in the evening
questions[7].optionsTranslation[1]: three a day, morning, noon and evening
